intended_object: For a simplicial set X and a subcomplex A ⊆ X, the set of nondegenerate simplices of X (of any dimension) that do not lie in A. This comes from the docstring.
explanation:
The structure extends `X.N`. A term of `X.N` is a simplex of X of some dimension n (that is, a term of `X.S`: a dimension together with an element of X _⦋n⦌) along with a proof that it is nondegenerate. `SSet.Subcomplex.N` adds one condition: the simplex does not belong to `A.obj _`, the n-simplices of the subcomplex. So its terms are exactly the nondegenerate simplices of X that are not in A, as the docstring says. This set indexes the nondegenerate cells of the relative complex (X, A).

The definition is stated for an arbitrary simplicial set and an arbitrary subcomplex, which is the natural generality. No other Mathlib declaration defines this object; this definition is itself the Mathlib version.
